name: Biz Markie
hook: A human beatbox and comic rapper whose unlicensed sample lost the court case that ended hip-hop's free-sampling era.
blurb: Marcel Hall was born in Harlem and grew up on Long Island. As Biz Markie he was part of the Juice Crew around Marley Marl, and his first record, in 1986, showed off his beatboxing: drum sounds made with his mouth. 'Just a Friend' in 1989 was a big hit, a reminder that the Juice Crew made room for comedy and beatboxing alongside its hardest records. In 1991 his album I Need a Haircut used a looped piece of Gilbert O'Sullivan's song 'Alone Again (Naturally)'. Permission had been asked for, refused, and ignored. O'Sullivan sued and won in Grand Upright Music v. Warner Bros. Records (1991). The judgment treated sampling without a licence as plain infringement, referred the matter for possible criminal prosecution, and ordered the album taken out of the shops, and hip-hop producers have had to get permission for samples ever since. Biz named his next album, in 1993, All Samples Cleared!, which is itself a record of the new rules. He died in July 2021, aged 57.
